items.title: Why is pepper such a popular spice? - Carolyn Beans
items.author: TED-Ed
items.content:
<article>Trace the history of pepper, and explore how this seasoning shaped empires to become one of the world's most popular spices.

--

Thousands of years ago, people on the Malabar Coast began growing Piper nigrum, the black pepper plant. Early migrants and traders helped move pepper from India to Indonesia and beyond, with Egypt, China, and Rome being some of the earliest adopters. And today, black pepper makes up 20% of the global spice trade. So, what makes the spice so popular? Carolyn Beans traces the seasoning's history.

Lesson by Carolyn Beans, directed by Thomas Volda.

items.title: Is salt the most important ingredient in history? - Carolyn Beans
items.author: TED-Ed
items.content:
<article>Trace the influence of salt throughout human history, and explore how this essential seasoning shaped our civilizations.

--

As early as the 1st millennium CE, humans began harvesting salt to trade. In ancient civilizations, salt wasn’t just a biological necessity, but an essential tool that allowed them to preserve fish, meats, produce, and dairy. And it was also prized for making food taste better. So, how did this simple mineral change human history? Carolyn Beans traces the influence of this essential seasoning.

Lesson by Carolyn Beans, directed by Ivana Volda.

items.title: Can you solve the Billy Bonka riddle? - Edwin F. Meyer
items.author: TED-Ed
items.content:
<article>You accidentally end up in the top secret lab of an eccentric candy factory. Can you win Billy Bonka's game and get set free?

--

You’re on a tour of the eccentric Billy Bonka’s mysterious candy factory, when a wrong turn searching for the restroom lands you in the top secret candy laboratory. Enraged at your trespassing, Bonka explains that the consequences are simple: you must play his game. You lose, and he’ll throw you into his Chew-o-meter 3000. Can you outsmart Billy Bonka’s challenge? Edwin F. Meyer shows how.

Lesson by Edwin F. Meyer, directed by Igor Ćorić, Artrake Studio.

items.title: What if you didn’t brush your teeth for a year? - Justin Merritt
items.author: TED-Ed
items.content:
<article>Trace the impact that not brushing or flossing can have on your teeth, gums, microbiome, and overall health over time.

--

At any given time, your mouth is maintaining a delicate balance between hundreds of microbial species, which is why dentists agree that you should brush twice and floss once every day. But what if you just… didn’t? If you stopped doing any oral hygiene, how long would it take for your mouth to get messy? Justin Merritt investigates how not brushing can impact your health over time.

Lesson by Justin Merritt, directed by Lee Oz, Eliška Oz, Oz Animation.

items.title: 5 sneaky ways stores get you to spend more
items.author: TED-Ed
items.content:
<article>Explore 5 tactics that retailers use to influence what you buy and what you’re willing to pay, and how to avoid being tricked.

--

You’re about to buy some bargain bin headphones when you spot another sale. A different pair that is more expensive, but selling for half their usual price. Which is the better buy? And how do you know you’re not falling for a retailer’s psychological tricks? Explore common tactics that retailers use to influence what you buy and what you’re willing to pay, and how you can avoid being tricked.

Directed by Homework Studio.

items.title: Why does this animal never age? - Raymond Adkins
items.author: TED-Ed
items.content:
<article>Explore the incredible regenerative abilities of hydras, and get to know their biology to find out if they're really immortal. 

--

In 1740, naturalist Abraham Trembley found something shocking in pondwater. He couldn't tell if it was a plant or an animal, though its way of moving and consuming things seemed animal-like. But when he cut parts off or even split it in two, it regenerated, which was decidedly plant-like. So, what was this miraculous creature? Raymond Adkins explores the near-immortal biology of the hydra.

Lesson by Raymond Adkins, directed by Sharon Colman.
